title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The title and outlet record that a Minnesota lawyer was suspended in connection with fake AI-generated case citations, a pattern seen in other jurisdictions where a generative AI system produced plausible-looking but nonexistent legal citations that were then submitted to a court without independent verification. This is a known failure mode: a language model asserting fabricated information as fact, combined with a deployment context, legal practice, where a human check against primary sources would have been the standard safeguard.

The failure occurs at the point of use rather than inside the model itself. A practitioner relying on AI-generated output without verifying each citation against an actual legal database removes the only layer that could catch hallucinated references before they reach a court filing.

What the underlying article actually says is not established, because the source text provided contained no article body, only navigation elements and unrelated headlines. The suspension is reported in the title, but the specific citations involved, the AI system used, and the precise procedural consequences are not confirmed by any content available here.
